newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Daewoo hits year high on earnings prospects.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo hits year high on earnings prospects.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Daewoo Electronics SA leapt nearly 14 percent in busy dealings on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, lifted by expectations of strong earnings, dealers and analysts said on Monday.

They said the earnings potential stemmed from a sharp reduction in the group's debt, the restructure of its white goods operations to cut low margin products and a return to profitability by its television and video business.

"But the big kicker is the joint venture between Multichoice and Daewoo to rent satellite equipment. It is performing very strongly and will continue to do so over the next few years," said Anthony Clark, small companies analyst at Standard Equities.
Daewoo shares on Monday rose 41 cents to a high of 335 cents -- its best level this year -- in a volume of 237,600 shares.
Clark told Reuters he expected Daewoo to show earnings growth of nearly 90 percent a share to 12.0 cents in the year to end-December, rising to over 20.0 cents the following year.
Clark said the firm was now debt free following a 60 million rand preference share issue and a 15 million rand rebate from the Receiver of Revenue.

The expected improvement follows a tough previous 12 months to end-March when Daewoo's earnings fell four percent to 6.4 cents amid poor consumer demand for large household electrical goods, a hefty interest bill on high borrowings and pressure from illegal electrical imports.
Daewoo is due to report half year results early in September.
